entities.summary:
Pierre Desceliers (fl. 1530s-1560s) was a French cartographer and a key figure of the Dieppe School of Cartography. His cartographic works, such as 'La Carte de Pierre Desceliers' (1530s), showcased his expertise in hydrography and geography. Desceliers' contributions to the field of cartography were significant, as he was one of the first to accurately map the coastlines of France and the Netherlands.

Desceliers' work also had a lasting impact on the development of navigation and maritime trade. His maps were used by sailors and explorers, including Jacques Cartier, who credited Desceliers' work for his discoveries in North America. The French monarch, Francis I, also recognized Desceliers' contributions, appointing him as the royal cartographer in 1554.

Today, Pierre Desceliers is remembered as the father of French hydrography, and his cartographic works are considered some of the most important in the history of the field. His legacy can be seen in the continued use of his maps and the influence of his work on modern cartography.

'La Carte de Pierre Desceliers' is a testament to his enduring legacy, and its accurate depiction of the French coastline remains a valuable resource for historians and scholars today.
